practices.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and do not commit real credentials to the repo; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.

Connect to the cluster using the provided URI with mongoose.connect(...) and then select the intended database with connection.useDb('sample_customer_360_01') so all sample operations are scoped to the designated DB.
Avoid hardcoding TLS/SSL flags in code; rely on the provided connection string and current driver defaults for required TLS options.
Create a unique index on customerId (CustomerSchema.index({ customerId: 1 }, { unique: true })) so identity resolution and upserts can rely on a stable unique key.
Create indexes in an idempotent, non-destructive way (call createIndexes and handle IndexKeySpecsConflict rather than dropping existing indexes), as done in the seed script.
Perform single-document idempotent upserts using updateOne with upsert:true and $set/$setOnInsert (set updatedAt and setOnInsert createdAt) to keep writes atomic and safe for concurrent updates.
Model each source system as a nested subdocument (sources.crm, sources.ecommerce, sources.support) so source-specific attributes are stored under each source key.
Use a flexible SourceSchema (strict: false) for source subdocuments so events with different attribute shapes can be accepted without prior schema changes.
Provide seed and verify scripts that operate only in the designated sample database (sample_customer_360_01) and implement idempotent behavior for safe repeated runs.
Validate incoming event shape at the API boundary and return HTTP 400 for missing required fields to avoid invalid writes (require source, customerId, attributes).
